clarifications: Task scope is strictly 5 budget-counted files.
Normal G-031 limit of 5 files is observed with zero overrides.
G-041 semantic authorization is FALSE (zero semantic files modified).
G-042 guardrails authorization is FALSE (zero guardrails modified).
Canonical Weapon Action values are exactly READY, FIRING, and RELOADING. The TypeScript const object, union type, and runtime helpers are implementation choices.

READY is represented only as an approved value; T-013 does not infer ammo availability, firing permission, cooldown completion, input readiness, unstunned state, global actionability, or universal initial state. No READY state factory is created.

No WeaponActionState container or wrapper is implemented. There is currently insufficient canonical transition authority to safely construct active FIRING or RELOADING state containers. T-013 remains value-only for Weapon Action.
No Weapon Action transitions (beginFiring, stopFiring, beginReload, etc.) are implemented; no public API puts a character into FIRING or RELOADING as executable combat state.

Posture-side firing prerequisite is implemented as a pure query: doesPostureSatisfyFiringPrerequisite(posture). EXPOSED returns true; COVERED, TRANSITIONING_TO_COVERED, and TRANSITIONING_TO_EXPOSED return false.

Critical authority boundary: A result of true means strictly that the Character Posture satisfies the canonical posture-side prerequisite for firing. It does NOT mean actual firing begins, character can globally fire, is globally eligible, is globally actionable, or action becomes FIRING. Actual firing remains subject to additional unmodeled/deferred axes (weapon/ammo state, control state, firing intent/input routing, cadence/timing). T-013 neither evaluates nor defines their complete conjunction.
Character Posture and Weapon Action remain separate domain vocabularies/types; semantic orthogonality is not asserted via runtime string comparisons.
No Object.freeze runtime immutability semantics are introduced. as const provides compile-time narrowing and is not tested as runtime freezing.
T-011 EventBatch, executeEventBatch, EffectIntent, and Derived Events are not used.
Weapon Action domain event taxonomy remains deferred.

Metadata preservation: getDomainState() preserves gameplayImplemented: false because false is the existing Human-Trusted value, the lifecycle semantics for changing it to true are not formally defined, and T-013 has no authority to redefine that metadata meaning.
